newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - March 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - March 27.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- TRADE DEFICIT FALLS TO LOWEST LEVEL FOR MORE THAN A YEAR

Strong growth in exports to the US, achieved in spite of the strength of the pound, helped the UK's trade deficit to fall to its lowest level for over a year in January. Figures from the Office for National Statistics show that the UK's trade deficit with the rest of the world fell from 825 million stg in December to 641 million sterling in January. The underlying deficit, which excludes oil and erratic items such as ships and aircraft, shows an even greater improvement in January, falling from 1.94 billion stg to 1.32 billion stg. However, the figures also showed signs of rising imports and falling exports, which could cause the UK's trade deficit to grow if sterling remains strong.
-- ROME AGREES TO BUDGET MOVE TO MEET TARGETS FOR EMU

Italy's centre-left government will today unveil a package of measures designed to correct a budget deficit 0.8 per cent greater than the ceiling of 3 per cent of GDP laid down by the Maastricht treaty. With only a third of the package coming from spending cuts, the mini-budget, which was approved by the governing coalition parties Wednesday, relies heavily on accounting devices to raise the L15,300bn required to meet the Emu target. Almost half of the shortfall will be obtained from funds which companies are obliged to set aside for paying employees who leave. Giulio Tremonti, the finance expert of the right-wing opposition, described the move as a "tax on productivity and jobs which will create unemployment".
-- NIREX MAY GO TO COURT OVER PLANNING SNUB

Nirex, the nuclear waste storage company, is considering whether to mount a legal challenge to the dismissal of its application to construct an underground laboratory at Sellafield. The board of the company is to meet on Thursday to make a decision on legal action following the decision by environment secretary John Gummer last week to uphold a ruling by Cumbria County Council not to allow planning permission for the 200 million stg research facility, which would have been used to assess whether the area was suitable for a 1.9 billion stg nuclear dump.
-- WATCHDOG SMOOTHS WAY FOR DIGITAL TELEVISION

Telecoms industry regulator Don Cruickshank has written to the principal players likely to be involved in the introduction of digital television in the UK to assess their preparations for the new technology and to ensure they do not fall foul of regulatory guidelines published on Wednesday. The technology provides the potential for viewers to access up to 200 channels of television via a special 'set-top box', and the main companies involved include the BBC, BSkyB and British Telecom as well as the cable television groups.
-- AVIS EUROPE IN 267 MILLION STG RETURN TO LONDON

Avis Europe, the car hire group, has taken advantage of the favourable new issue market in Britain with a second appearance on the London stock market in just over a decade. Avis, Europe's largest car hire group, returned to the stock market with the offer of 215 million shares priced at 124p. The stock moved to an immediate premium to close at 131.5p. An earlier Avis issue in 1986 saw almost two thirds of the shares left with the underwriters. Wednesday's offer, which represented 36.9 per cent of the equity, raised 267 million stg and valued the group at 722 million stg.
-- BIOCOMPATIBLES IN $12 MILLION PURCHASE OF TECHNOLOGY

Fast-growing medical devices company Biocompatibles International has paid $12 million (7.4 million stg) to acquire Surfacine, an anti-bacterial coating technology. Biocompatibles bought the new technology from US healthcare group Biopolymetrix. News of the deal came as Biocompatibles announced increased losses in 1996, to 18.5 million stg, following an increase in spending on research and development. Turnover rose from 3.8 million stg to 11 million stg.
-- WAL-MART PLANS BIG ON-LINE EXPANSION

Retail giant Wal-Mart Stores has announced plans for a massive expansion of its Internet shopping operation in the US. Wal-Mart, the world's biggest retailer, aims to more than double the number of items available on-line to about 80,000 by the year-end. The move represents the growing enthusiasm over the prospects for on-line shopping, with Wal-Mart expanding its operation rapidly since its launch last July with just 2,500 items on offer.
-- TRUCKS HOLD UP DAWSONGROUP

Dawsongroup, the truck and trailer hire company, has reported a 12 per cent fall in 1996 profits following stiff competition and weak demand in the truck rental market. A 19 per cent fall in truck hire revenue prompted a decline in underlying profits of 36 per cent, to 7.2 million stg. The group has reduced its dependence on truck hire from 66 per cent of revenues in 1993 to 50 per cent last year, and says it will continue to diversify into higher-growth areas such as cold storage and trailer hire.
-- PIRELLI BEATS FORECASTS AND DOUBLES DIVIDEND

Pirelli, the Italian cables and tyres group, has reported a 43 per cent increase in consolidated net profits inn 1996, to L436 billion ($258 million). The results, which were ahead of analyst's forecasts, follow the restructuring of the company after its near-collapse in 1991. The new Pirelli, under the stewardship of chairman Marco Tronchetti Provera, concentrates on its core tyre and cables businesses as well as on the development of high-performance, high-margin products.
-- STET INVESTORS APPROVE GOLDEN SHARE

Shareholders in Italian group Stet have approved the introduction of a golden share in the state-controlled telecommunications group, allowing the government a veto on important decisions such as mergers, acquisitions or disposals following this year's privatisation. The move may placate the Refounded Communists, who are opposed to the full privatisation of Stet and whose support the Italian government needs.
